response.passage: In the bustling markets of Delhi, Mr. Sharma often buys packaged snacks for his family. He recently learned that reading food labels is essential for health. A label lists ingredients in descending order by weight, meaning the first item is the most abundant. For instance, if a biscuit packet lists sugar before flour, it contains more sugar than flour. Nutritionist Dr. Anjali Gupta explains that high sodium levels, often exceeding 400 milligrams per serving, can lead to increased blood pressure. Because excessive salt causes hypertension, many health-conscious parents now check the 'Sodium' line carefully. Some labels use the term 'Natural Flavors,' which does not always mean the ingredients are organic or healthy. In 2022, a survey in Mumbai showed that only 15 percent of shoppers read these labels thoroughly. Understanding these details helps consumers like Mr. Sharma make better choices. By ignoring marketing claims on the front of the pack and focusing on the back, shoppers can avoid hidden additives. It is a simple habit that protects long-term well-being for everyone in India.
response.summary: Reading food labels helps consumers identify the main ingredients and sodium content in packaged snacks. By checking the back of the pack instead of marketing claims, shoppers can make healthier food choices.
